chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya, who said:
He said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The time for Asr prayer is until the setting of the sun.'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Asr prayer end according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), transmitted via the chain of Sa'd ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, clarifies the definition of Asr's time as extending until sunset, a view often associated with the time of necessity (waqt al-darura) or the broader definition in Shia jurisprudence. It appears in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on prayer times, highlighting the scholarly discourse on whether Asr ends at the yellowing of the sun or at actual sunset. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the duration of the afternoon prayer.
